description: Boosting Community Storm Resilience in Alaska is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA Office for Costal Management Digital Coast. Many remote coastal communities in Alaska currently have no formal storm history data, flood risk analysis, or way to predict and assess flooding impacts to their communities. These communities are at risk of flooding due to climate change and other coastal hazards such as storms. Coverage: Alaska (2022). The toolkit gives Alaska as the location, 2022 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
